title: A new way to think about a repo
what: Not a pile of files and commits: living lines, each with its own author and history, that close back up as plain git whenever you like.

title: Multiplayer, every which way
what: Human to human, human to AI, AI to AI: everyone in the same repo at once, live, line by line, and every line says who.

title: Own your git history
what: Every line, author and rev is yours, in a real git repo you can clone anywhere. Nobody upstream gets a say.

title: A repo that builds itself
what: Its code, its deploy config, its dependency doctor and its agents in one place: agents propose on branches, the doctor keeps it fresh, previews prove it, and your commit ships it.

title: Buy into Rusty Buns, deploy all over
what: One config ships the same app as a desktop binary, a Cloudflare Worker, and a server on Hetzner or Railway.

title: Edit live, together
what: Lines have stable ids, so agents editing different lines never collide. Edits stream to every open page.

title: Private lines in a public repo
what: Hide some lines from everyone but the crew: on the page, in blame, in shares, and blank in git.

title: Share some lines, not the repo
what: A live link to a range that follows those lines as the file changes, even from a private repo.

title: Public or private repos
what: A private repo you can't see answers 404, in search too.

title: Time travel
what: Replay a file to any edit it ever had, with blame per line.

title: Cut
what: Some lines plus everything they use, as their own branch: run the tests, then merge the fix back.

title: The dependency doctor
what: Proposes safe updates on a branch, tests them in a throwaway clone, and can have an agent fix what broke.

title: Runs on a laptop too
what: The same app runs as a desktop binary, with sqlite standing in for D1 and git on disk standing in for Artifacts.

title: A file is a Durable Object
what: Each file has one writer, so every edit from every person and agent lands in one order.

title: See who's here
what: Presence shows who else has the file open, as they type.

title: Every line knows who wrote it
what: Author and time on every line, people and agents alike.

title: Branches and merges, by line
what: A three-way merge by line id: moved blocks keep their edits, and real conflicts are named one stretch at a time.

title: Build changes get a second look
what: A branch that touches package.json, lockfiles or deploy config waits for “I've read the build changes”.

title: Closes up as a real git commit
what: Cataloguing pushes a real commit to Cloudflare Artifacts, built by hand: no git library.

title: Clone it with plain git
what: Every repo has a git clone line with a read token that lasts an hour.

title: Levels
what: Small, well-loved repos (mitt, clsx, Ky, Zustand, Hono, Express, Preact) to browse and fork.

title: Dig up any GitHub repo
what: Paste a URL, a remote or a gh repo clone line and fork it into a git repo you own. Upstream never hears about it.

title: Share cards for X
what: A cut's code and its test result, drawn into a PNG inside the Worker with no image library.

title: Put a coding agent on a file
what: claude, codex, pi or opencode edit a file, and their lines land live, blamed on the agent.

title: Rusty Buns fit
what: Every repo page says how easily it ships as a desktop binary, a Worker and a server.

title: Deploy for real
what: Ship the repo's stack to a stage you pick. Only a person ships; agents never start a deploy.

title: Webhooks for CI/CD
what: GitHub-shaped JSON, signed with HMAC-SHA256, logged, and retried when it fails.

title: One command palette, one API
what: Press ⌘K. Every action is one API call, shown next to it, so people and agents do the same things the same way.

title: Search code
what: Full-text search over everything committed that you're allowed to see.

title: Playlists of code
what: Collect line ranges you love from any file you can see. Each track follows its lines as they change.

title: Your profile is your own HTML
what: Write your own HTML and CSS, sandboxed, no scripts.

title: Sign in your way
what: GitHub, Google, or email and password, and a handle that's yours for good.

title: Rate limits that queue
what: Over the cap, a dig waits its turn in line instead of failing, and finds you on your profile when it's done.

title: Same line? Retry, don't clobber
what: Two edits to one line can't both win: the stale one gets a 409 and retries. An edit that depends on the whole file only lands if nothing moved since it was read.

title: Merges that know the file
what: A lockfile conflicts whole, a config key can't land twice, lines added beside deleted code are flagged, and the merged files must still build before they land.

title: Your mods, marked
what: A fork says where it came from and at which commit. Every line you changed is marked; the rest are blamed on upstream.

title: Private GitHub repos, on the desktop
what: Dig up your own private repos with your GitHub login, passed to git for the one clone and never written into the repo.

title: Big repos, small bills
what: A file only becomes a Durable Object when someone opens it, and a commit pushes only what changed: one edited line costs one blob.

title: Visitors' digs clean up after themselves
what: A visitor's fork lasts a day, and only so many live at once, so nobody's experiment runs up the bill.

title: Test results in the gutter
what: A cut's test run marks each test's line pass or fail, and every line a failure's stack points at.

title: Agents that redo their work
what: If someone changes a line an agent also changed, it runs again on the new text. A rename changes every use in one batch.

title: Agents in their own containers
what: On Cloudflare each agent run gets its own container, with only its own CLI's keys, stopped the moment it's done.

title: Built for agents that get prompt-injected
what: Agents work on branches and never deploy, so anything an injection plants waits for a person to read it.

title: Updates that have aged
what: The doctor skips releases younger than 3 days, regenerates lockfiles with install scripts off, and reads private registries from .npmrc.

title: Preview deploys
what: Spin up a throwaway preview of the repo before anything ships, logged like every deploy.

title: Ship when you commit
what: Turn it on and your own commits to main deploy. A commit mid-deploy ships once more afterwards.

title: Deploy keys that never come back out
what: Write-only, sealed in D1 under AES-GCM, shown only by their last 4, scrubbed from output, and kept from agent containers.

title: Production is a choice
what: A stack that takes over live resources only ships once the owner marks the repo as production.

title: Every deploy on the record
what: Who, which commit, which stage, the result and the end of its output, for the last 50 deploys and previews.

title: Monorepos welcome
what: Point deploys and previews at the app's own folder inside a bigger repo.

title: Agents from your shell
what: bun agent.ts does what the Agent button does, so a script or another agent can drive one.

title: A binary for every desktop
what: macOS (arm64 and x64), Linux (x64 and arm64) and Windows, cross-compiled from one machine.

title: Secrets from 1Password, behind Touch ID
what: Deploy secrets come through varlock straight into the Worker. The repo commits names and references, never values.

title: Plan first, always
what: A deploy refuses unless you planned this exact config, lists every billable resource first, and won't start a big server unless you allow it.

title: Takes over what's already live
what: Adopts an existing Worker and D1 by name, storage intact, instead of making new ones.

title: An API for outside agents
what: An OpenAPI spec of every command, and personal API tokens that act as you, read-only or not, always expiring, never an admin.
